title: Invertible modules descend along affine transition limits
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact schemes [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] that are quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], with affine transition morphisms $q_{ji}:Z_j\to Z_i$ for $j\geq i$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ with projections $q_i:Z\to Z_i$ be its limit in the category of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Here being a limit means $q_{ji}\circ q_j=q_i$ for $j\geq i$, and for every scheme $T$ and family $t_i:T\to Z_i$ satisfying $q_{ji}\circ t_j=t_i$ there is a unique morphism $t:T\to Z$ with $q_i\circ t=t_i$ for every $i$. For every invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], there exist $i\in I$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$-module $L_i$ such that $q_i^*L_i\cong L$, where $q_i^*$ is the tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: Set $N=L^\vee$. By [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible], $N$ is invertible and evaluation is an isomorphism $e:L\otimes N\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_Z$. Both $L$ and $N$ have finite presentation: by [def-sc-invertible-module] each is locally $\mathcal O_Z$, which has the finite presentation $0\to\mathcal O_Z\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_Z\to0$. No finiteness of a chosen trivializing cover is needed here.

source.place: Tag 0B8W, lemma-descend-invertible-modules, proof of (2), tensor inverse; modules.tex Tag 01CT, lemma-constructions-invertible, clause (2).

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-trf-fp-modules-affine-limit-descent] separately to $L$ and $N$. Choose a common upper bound $i$ of the two indices, and pull both models to $Z_i$; call them $A_i,B_i$. By [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation] these remain finitely presented. The composition isomorphisms of [def-pc-module-pullback] give specified isomorphisms $q_i^*A_i\cong L$ and $q_i^*B_i\cong N$. All hypotheses of the descent statement are precisely the assumed small nonempty directed indexing set, qcqs stages, affine transitions and scheme limit; no stage is assumed affine or Noetherian.

source.place: Tags 01ZR, lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation (1), and 0B8W, lemma-descend-invertible-modules, proof of (2); modules.tex Tag 01BQ for preservation under pullback.

proof.text:
Put $P_i=A_i\otimes B_i$. This is finitely presented, directly from local presentations. On a common open where $A_i=\operatorname{coker}(a:\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s)$ and $B_i=\operatorname{coker}(b:\mathcal O^t\to\mathcal O^u)$, it has presentation
$$\mathcal O^{ru}\oplus\mathcal O^{st}\xrightarrow{(a\otimes1,\,1\otimes b)}\mathcal O^{su}\longrightarrow P_i\longrightarrow0.$$
Indeed, a map out of the displayed cokernel is a bilinear map on the two free generating modules killing each family of relations; it therefore factors uniquely through $A_i\otimes B_i$. This is the tensor product defined in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with cokernels as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus the presentation is valid as a sheaf presentation, not a claim that sections of every cokernel are computed without sheafification. Also $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$ is finitely presented by its rank-one free presentation. This writes out the elementary presentation argument of Modules Tag 01CE(4).

source.place: Tag 01CE, lemma-tensor-product-permanence (4), explicit presentation in the proof.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor], the chosen model isomorphisms and evaluation define an isomorphism $\epsilon:q_i^*P_i\xrightarrow{\sim}q_i^*\mathcal O_{Z_i}$. Here $q_i^*\mathcal O_{Z_i}\cong\mathcal O_Z$ is the multiplication isomorphism $\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{q_i^{-1}\mathcal O_{Z_i}}q_i^{-1}\mathcal O_{Z_i}\cong\mathcal O_Z$ from the tensor-pullback definition [def-pc-module-pullback]. Apply clause (2) of [lem-trf-fp-modules-affine-limit-descent] to $\epsilon$ and separately to $\epsilon^{-1}$. At a common upper bound $j\geq i$ their pullbacks are maps $u_j:P_j\to Q_j$ and $v_j:Q_j\to P_j$, where $P_j=q_{ji}^*P_i$ and $Q_j=q_{ji}^*\mathcal O_{Z_i}$. Their limit pullbacks are $\epsilon$ and $\epsilon^{-1}$, with the canonical composition identifications; hence $q_j^*(v_j\circ u_j)=1$ and $q_j^*(u_j\circ v_j)=1$. The four finite-presentation hypotheses used here are those proved in step 3 and their pullbacks, covered by [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 0B8W, lemma-descend-invertible-modules, proof of (2), descent of evaluation; Tag 01ZR, lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation (2); modules.tex Tag 01CD for the tensor comparison.

proof.text: Apply clause (3) of [lem-trf-fp-modules-affine-limit-descent] to the endomorphism pair $v_j\circ u_j,1_{P_j}$, and again to $u_j\circ v_j,1_{Q_j}$. Choose a common upper bound $k\geq j$ of the two resulting stages. Pullback preserves identities and composition, so both equalities hold at $k$. Thus $u_k$ and $v_k$ are inverse maps and $q_{ki}^*P_i\cong q_{ki}^*\mathcal O_{Z_i}\cong\mathcal O_{Z_k}$. The source and target modules in both applications are finitely presented by step 3 and [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation]. This is the explicit reason the descended evaluation becomes an isomorphism; invertibility is not assumed to be reflected by a single projection to the limit.

source.place: Tag 0B8W, lemma-descend-invertible-modules, proof of (2), eventual isomorphism; Tag 01ZR, lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation (3).

proof.text: Set $L_k=q_{ki}^*A_i$ and $N_k=q_{ki}^*B_i$. The tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] identifies $L_k\otimes N_k$ with $q_{ki}^*P_i$, which step 5 identified with $\mathcal O_{Z_k}$. Apply exactly the tensor-inverse characterization explicitly included in [def-sc-invertible-module]: existence of an $\mathcal O_{Z_k}$-module $N_k$ with this tensor isomorphism means that $L_k$ is invertible. This uses that characterization, not the invalid assertion that a finitely presented module is already locally free. Finally [def-pc-module-pullback] gives $q_k^*L_k\cong q_i^*A_i\cong L$, since $q_{ki}\circ q_k=q_i$. Taking $k,L_k$ proves the claimed existence.

source.place: Tag 0B8W, lemma-descend-invertible-modules, final sentence of proof of (2); modules.tex Tags 0B8K, lemma-invertible, and 0B8M, lemma-invertible-is-locally-free-rank-1, as incorporated in def-sc-invertible-module.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B8W, lemma-descend-invertible-modules, proof of (2), using Tag 01ZR. Descend finite-presentation tensor factors directly; finite-local-freeness/flatness descent is unnecessary because the tensor-inverse characterization is already in def-sc-invertible-module. The map, inverse and two identities are all descended explicitly.
